### Acid–Base Chemistry

Groups: 2 · Skills: 7

[acidBaseChemistry.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/acidBaseChemistry/acidBaseChemistry.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Acid–base chemistry concerns proton transfer, electron-pair interactions, acidity, and the behavior of chemical systems under relevant conditions. Its models, solution properties, transformations and analytical methods are broader than reaction-pattern classification alone.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how acids and bases interact and how chemists describe and measure acidity.

#### Acid–Base Fundamentals

Skills: 3

[acidBaseFundamentals.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/acidBaseChemistry/acidBaseFundamentals/acidBaseFundamentals.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Conceptual acid–base models establish what counts as an acid or base, while strength and pH describe different aspects of chemical behavior and solution conditions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand different acid–base models, acidity, and acid strength.

##### Acid–Base Models

[acidBaseModels.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/acidBaseChemistry/acidBaseFundamentals/skills/acidBaseModels.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish common Arrhenius, Brønsted–Lowry and Lewis descriptions by the chemical interactions each includes.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare how common chemical models define an acid or a base.

##### Acid Strength

[acidStrength.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/acidBaseChemistry/acidBaseFundamentals/skills/acidStrength.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Describe how strongly an acid tends to donate a proton under specified conditions. A stronger acid transfers protons more readily in a comparable system; this does not mean the solution is necessarily more concentrated or more hazardous.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish an acid's strength from how concentrated or hazardous its solution is.

##### pH

[pH.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/acidBaseChemistry/acidBaseFundamentals/skills/pH.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret a logarithmic measure of hydrogen-ion activity and its concentration-based approximations.

**User-friendly description (en):** Read pH as a logarithmic way to describe acidity in a solution.

#### Acid–Base Systems

Skills: 4

[acidBaseSystems.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/acidBaseChemistry/acidBaseSystems/acidBaseSystems.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Neutralization, indicator responses, buffer equilibria and titration exemplify how acid–base behavior is observed, controlled and measured under specific conditions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how acids and bases react and how their effects are measured.

##### Acid–Base Indicators

[acidBaseIndicators.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/acidBaseChemistry/acidBaseSystems/skills/acidBaseIndicators.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why some compounds change observable properties as solution acidity varies.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how indicators change appearance as acidity changes.

##### Acid–Base Titration

[acidBaseTitration.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/acidBaseChemistry/acidBaseSystems/skills/acidBaseTitration.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use a measured equivalence relationship to infer an unknown amount or concentration.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use acid–base titration measurements to determine an unknown amount.

##### Buffer Solutions

[bufferSolutions.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/acidBaseChemistry/acidBaseSystems/skills/bufferSolutions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how paired acid–base species resist moderate pH changes.

**User-friendly description (en):** See how buffer mixtures help resist changes in pH.

##### Neutralization

[neutralization.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/acidBaseChemistry/acidBaseSystems/skills/neutralization.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain net acid–base reactions and avoid assuming every neutralization gives a final pH of seven.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore why reacting an acid with a base does not always produce a neutral pH.

### Atoms and Periodicity

Groups: 5 · Skills: 21

[atomsAndPeriodicity.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/atomsAndPeriodicity.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The organization and electronic structure of atoms underpin elemental identity, isotopes, ions and recurring chemical behavior. This domain describes atomic constituents and trends; bond formation is treated separately.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore the particles inside atoms and the patterns connecting chemical elements.

#### Atomic Structure

Skills: 4

[atomicStructure.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/atomicStructure/atomicStructure.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Chemical element identity is determined by proton number; other atomic characteristics vary independently.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn what determines an element's identity and how atoms of the same element can differ.

##### Atomic Mass

[atomicMass.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/atomicStructure/skills/atomicMass.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret atomic mass and relative atomic mass, including why a tabulated average may not be a whole number.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore why average atomic masses are not always whole numbers.

##### Electrons and Charge

[electronsAndCharge.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/atomicStructure/skills/electronsAndCharge.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate electron gain or loss to ionic charge while preserving an element's identity.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain how losing or gaining electrons changes an atom's charge.

##### Neutrons and Isotopes

[neutronsAndIsotopes.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/atomicStructure/skills/neutronsAndIsotopes.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate neutron count to isotopic identity without treating isotopes as different elements.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand why isotopes of an element have different neutron numbers.

##### Protons and Atomic Number

[protonsAndAtomicNumber.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/atomicStructure/skills/protonsAndAtomicNumber.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use proton count to establish elemental identity and locate an element in the periodic table.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use the number of protons to identify an element.

#### Electronic Structure

Skills: 5

[electronicStructure.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/electronicStructure/electronicStructure.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Electron occupancy and energetic organization help explain reactivity and the behavior of valence electrons.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn how electrons are arranged and why that affects chemical behavior.

##### Atomic Orbitals

[atomicOrbitals.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/electronicStructure/skills/atomicOrbitals.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret orbitals as probability-based descriptions of electron states and their occupancy rather than fixed electron trajectories.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand atomic orbitals as regions described by electron probabilities.

##### Electron Configurations

[electronConfigurations.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/electronicStructure/skills/electronConfigurations.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Represent electron occupation for atoms and ions, respecting the applicable filling rules and exceptions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Represent how electrons occupy states in atoms and ions.

##### Electron Shells

[electronShells.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/electronicStructure/skills/electronShells.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use shell organization and principal energy levels to explain patterns of electron distribution without treating shells as literal paths of electrons.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use electron shells to explain patterns without imagining fixed planetary orbits.

##### Ion Formation

[ionFormation.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/electronicStructure/skills/ionFormation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Predict plausible monatomic ion charges from electron gain or loss while recognizing chemical context.

**User-friendly description (en):** Predict common ion charges while accounting for the chemical setting.

##### Valence Electrons

[valenceElectrons.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/electronicStructure/skills/valenceElectrons.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use outer-electron arrangements to reason about common chemical behavior and bonding possibilities.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use outer electrons to explain similarities in how elements react.

#### Nuclear Chemistry

Skills: 4

[nuclearChemistry.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/nuclearChemistry/nuclearChemistry.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Changes within atomic nuclei alter nuclide identities rather than ordinary electron bonding. The chemical emphasis is isotopic substances, decay and analytical applications; general nuclear-force physics belongs to Physics.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how changes to atomic nuclei differ from ordinary chemical reactions.

##### Half-Life

[halfLife.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/nuclearChemistry/skills/halfLife.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret the characteristic decay time of a radioactive population without implying that individual nuclei have predictable lifetimes.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand half-life as a pattern for many radioactive atoms, not a clock for one atom.

##### Isotope Tracers

[isotopeTracers.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/nuclearChemistry/skills/isotopeTracers.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how detectable isotopic signatures can trace material pathways or provide chemical analytical evidence.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how isotopes can help trace materials through chemical processes.

##### Nuclear Transmutation

[nuclearTransmutation.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/nuclearChemistry/skills/nuclearTransmutation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Account for changes in proton and nucleon number across nuclear reactions and decays.

**User-friendly description (en):** Track changes in proton and nucleon counts during nuclear transformations.

##### Radioactive Decay

[radioactiveDecay.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/nuclearChemistry/skills/radioactiveDecay.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish spontaneous nuclear transformation from chemical reaction, including emissions and daughter nuclides.

**User-friendly description (en):** Identify radioactive changes that transform one nuclide into another.

#### Periodic Organization

Skills: 4

[periodicOrganization.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/periodicOrganization/periodicOrganization.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The periodic table encodes repeating patterns in electron configurations and useful chemical categories.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how the periodic table organizes elements into useful patterns.

##### Element Families

[elementFamilies.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/periodicOrganization/skills/elementFamilies.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, halogens and noble gases to shared chemical tendencies.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize common tendencies of major periodic-table families.

##### Metals, Nonmetals and Metalloids

[metalsNonmetalsAndMetalloids.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/periodicOrganization/skills/metalsNonmetalsAndMetalloids.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use the broad distinctions and their limitations to infer plausible chemical and physical behavior.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish metals, nonmetals and metalloids while allowing for exceptions.

##### Periodic Table Structure

[periodicTableStructure.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/periodicOrganization/skills/periodicTableStructure.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret periods, groups and element symbols as an organized classification rather than a list ordered by bulk mass.

**User-friendly description (en):** Read the groups, periods and symbols of the periodic table.

##### Periodicity

[periodicity.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/periodicOrganization/skills/periodicity.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why some element properties recur as atomic number increases.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain why certain element properties repeat across the periodic table.

#### Periodic Trends

Skills: 4

[periodicTrends.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/periodicTrends/periodicTrends.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Atomic size and electrostatic attraction influence recurring patterns and their important exceptions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore trends in atomic size and attraction for electrons.

##### Atomic Radius Trends

[atomicRadiusTrends.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/periodicTrends/skills/atomicRadiusTrends.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain broad size trends across periods and down groups using nuclear charge and shielding.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare how atomic sizes change across the periodic table.

##### Electron Affinity

[electronAffinity.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/periodicTrends/skills/electronAffinity.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish electron-addition energetics from electronegativity and ionization energy.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish energy changes from electron attachment from other atomic trends.

##### Electronegativity

[electronegativity.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/periodicTrends/skills/electronegativity.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use relative electron-attracting tendency to reason about bonds and polarity.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use electronegativity to reason about how atoms share electrons.

##### Ionization Energy

[ionizationEnergy.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/atomsAndPeriodicity/periodicTrends/skills/ionizationEnergy.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret the energy needed to remove an electron and its relation to atomic structure.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand the energy required to remove an electron from an atom.

### Bonding and Structure

Groups: 3 · Skills: 12

[bondingAndStructure.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/bondingAndStructure/bondingAndStructure.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Chemical properties arise partly from how atoms and ions are connected and how neighboring particles interact. This domain distinguishes intraparticle bonds from interactions between particles and from bulk structural arrangements.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how chemical bonds and attractions between particles shape material properties.

#### Chemical Bonds

Skills: 4

[chemicalBonds.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/bondingAndStructure/chemicalBonds/chemicalBonds.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Different electron distributions support different limiting models of chemical bonding; real substances can have mixed characteristics.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how atoms and ions form chemical bonds with different electron arrangements.

##### Bond Polarity

[bondPolarity.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/bondingAndStructure/chemicalBonds/skills/bondPolarity.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use electronegativity differences to characterize unequal electron sharing without equating every polar bond with a polar molecule.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore why electrons can be shared unevenly in a chemical bond.

##### Covalent Bonding

[covalentBonding.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/bondingAndStructure/chemicalBonds/skills/covalentBonding.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain electron sharing in bonds between atoms, including differences between single and multiple bonds.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how atoms share electrons in single and multiple covalent bonds.

##### Ionic Bonding

[ionicBonding.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/bondingAndStructure/chemicalBonds/skills/ionicBonding.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain electrostatic attraction in extended ionic structures after electron transfer is represented conceptually.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain how opposite charges hold ions together in ionic structures.

##### Metallic Bonding

[metallicBonding.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/bondingAndStructure/chemicalBonds/skills/metallicBonding.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate delocalized electrons and ordered metal atoms to common metallic properties.

**User-friendly description (en):** Connect mobile electrons in metals with their characteristic properties.

#### Interparticle Interactions

Skills: 4

[interparticleInteractions.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/bondingAndStructure/interparticleInteractions/interparticleInteractions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Attractions between distinct particles influence phase behavior, solubility and material properties without changing covalent connectivity.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how particles attract one another without forming new chemical bonds.

##### Dipole Interactions

[dipoleInteractions.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/bondingAndStructure/interparticleInteractions/skills/dipoleInteractions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate permanent molecular polarity to orientation-dependent attractions between molecules.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how polar molecules attract one another according to their orientation.

##### Dispersion Forces

[dispersionForces.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/bondingAndStructure/interparticleInteractions/skills/dispersionForces.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain attractions arising from fluctuating electron distributions and their broad dependence on particle polarizability.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore the weak attractions caused by constantly shifting electron distributions.

##### Hydrogen Bonding

[hydrogenBonding.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/bondingAndStructure/interparticleInteractions/skills/hydrogenBonding.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize the conditions for stronger directional interactions involving hydrogen bound to suitable electronegative atoms.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when molecular structures can form hydrogen bonds.

##### Structure–Property Relationships

[structurePropertyRelationships.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/bondingAndStructure/interparticleInteractions/skills/structurePropertyRelationships.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use bonding and intermolecular interactions jointly to explain contrasting boiling points, hardness or conductivity.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use bonds and particle interactions to explain differences between materials.

#### Molecular and Extended Structure

Skills: 4

[molecularAndExtendedStructure.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/bondingAndStructure/molecularAndExtendedStructure/molecularAndExtendedStructure.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Spatial arrangement and connectedness influence substance behavior independently of a simple formula.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn how the arrangement of particles influences the behavior of materials.

##### Ionic Lattices

[ionicLattices.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/bondingAndStructure/molecularAndExtendedStructure/skills/ionicLattices.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate repeating ionic arrangements to melting behavior, brittleness and conduction conditions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Connect repeating ionic structures with brittleness, melting and electrical conduction.

##### Molecular Geometry

[molecularGeometry.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/bondingAndStructure/molecularAndExtendedStructure/skills/molecularGeometry.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Predict or interpret molecular shapes from electron-group arrangements and their limitations.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use electron arrangements to reason about the shapes of molecules.

##### Molecular Polarity

[molecularPolarity.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/bondingAndStructure/molecularAndExtendedStructure/skills/molecularPolarity.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Combine bond polarities with geometry to infer whether a molecule has a net dipole.

**User-friendly description (en):** Combine bond polarity and molecular shape to understand overall molecular polarity.

##### Network Solids

[networkSolids.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/bondingAndStructure/molecularAndExtendedStructure/skills/networkSolids.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Contrast extended covalent structures with discrete molecular solids using examples such as diamond and silica.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore why extended covalent networks behave differently from individual molecules.

### Chemical Inquiry

Groups: 4 · Skills: 19

[chemicalInquiry.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/chemicalInquiry.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Chemical knowledge connects observations of substances with explanations, testable models and reliable evidence. This domain covers chemistry-specific investigation and communication; general research methodology remains a cross-disciplinary concern.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how chemists investigate substances, test explanations and use trustworthy evidence.

#### Analytical Chemistry

Skills: 6

[analyticalChemistry.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/analyticalChemistry/analyticalChemistry.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Analytical chemistry identifies particular components in samples and determines their amounts. Sample treatment, chemical selectivity and calibration govern whether signals justify a conclusion; general observation and bulk property comparison are distinct competencies.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how chemists identify substances and measure their amounts in samples.

##### Analytical Interferences

[analyticalInterferences.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/analyticalChemistry/skills/analyticalInterferences.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify when other sample components alter a chemical signal or selective response and determine whether a method can distinguish the target analyte.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when other chemicals interfere with an analytical measurement.

##### Calibration Curves

[calibrationCurves.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/analyticalChemistry/skills/calibrationCurves.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate an instrument signal to known standards while recognizing background response, limited range and uncertainty.

**User-friendly description (en):** Read a calibration curve to connect instrument signals with known concentrations.

##### Qualitative Analyte Identification

[qualitativeAnalyteIdentification.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/analyticalChemistry/skills/qualitativeAnalyteIdentification.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use selective reactions or instrumental signatures to identify a target chemical species in a sample, recognizing that shared responses may prevent a unique identification.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use chemical tests or instrument signals to identify a substance in a mixture.

##### Quantitative Analyte Determination

[quantitativeAnalyteDetermination.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/analyticalChemistry/skills/quantitativeAnalyteDetermination.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Infer the amount or concentration of a specified analyte from a justified measured signal and calculation, accounting for relevant dilution or recovery factors.

**User-friendly description (en):** Determine how much of a target substance is present from appropriate measurements.

##### Sample Preparation for Analysis

[samplePreparationForAnalysis.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/analyticalChemistry/skills/samplePreparationForAnalysis.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Choose sample treatment, such as dissolution, extraction or dilution, to make a specified analyte measurable while considering contamination and analyte loss.

**User-friendly description (en):** Choose ways to prepare a sample while avoiding contamination or material loss.

##### Spectroscopic Evidence

[spectroscopicEvidence.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/analyticalChemistry/skills/spectroscopicEvidence.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret absorption, emission or related spectral patterns as information about chemical species, structure or concentration.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how spectra reveal clues about chemical identity, structure or amount.

#### Laboratory Reasoning

Skills: 4

[laboratoryReasoning.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/laboratoryReasoning/laboratoryReasoning.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Working with substances involves controlling exposure, maintaining traceability of samples and drawing conclusions that do not exceed the evidence.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn how to reason safely and draw justified conclusions when working with substances.

##### Chemical Handling Decisions

[chemicalHandlingDecisions.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/laboratoryReasoning/skills/chemicalHandlingDecisions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Choose risk-appropriate handling and disposal principles from substance identity, concentration and safety information rather than assuming familiar products are harmless.

**User-friendly description (en):** Choose safe handling principles based on chemical information and conditions.

##### Chemical Hazard Symbols

[chemicalHazardSymbols.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/laboratoryReasoning/skills/chemicalHazardSymbols.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret common chemical hazard pictograms and distinguish hazard from actual exposure and risk.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize chemical hazard symbols and understand that risk depends on exposure.

##### Evidence-Based Chemical Conclusions

[evidenceBasedChemicalConclusions.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/laboratoryReasoning/skills/evidenceBasedChemicalConclusions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Evaluate whether observations justify a claim about composition or reaction, including alternative explanations.

**User-friendly description (en):** Decide whether chemical observations really support a proposed explanation.

##### Experimental Variables

[experimentalVariables.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/laboratoryReasoning/skills/experimentalVariables.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish the manipulated chemical condition, observed response and controlled conditions in an investigation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Identify which chemical condition changes and what is measured in a fair investigation.

#### Measurements and Evidence

Skills: 5

[measurementsAndEvidence.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/measurementsAndEvidence/measurementsAndEvidence.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Chemical conclusions depend on measured quantities, recorded conditions and the distinction between observed patterns and explanatory claims.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how measurements and careful observation support chemical explanations.

##### Chemical Data Interpretation

[chemicalDataInterpretation.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/measurementsAndEvidence/skills/chemicalDataInterpretation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use tables and graphs to relate changing composition, time, temperature or measured property to chemical behavior.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use chemical data to explore relationships between conditions and outcomes.

##### Measurement Uncertainty

[measurementUncertainty.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/measurementsAndEvidence/skills/measurementUncertainty.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret the precision and uncertainty of experimental measurements rather than treating every reported digit as exact.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand why measured values have uncertainty rather than perfect precision.

##### Measuring Mass

[measuringMass.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/measurementsAndEvidence/skills/measuringMass.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Determine and interpret the mass of a sample, including appropriate units and the effects of container mass.

**User-friendly description (en):** Measure the mass of a sample while accounting for its container and units.

##### Measuring Volume

[measuringVolume.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/measurementsAndEvidence/skills/measuringVolume.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Determine liquid or gas volume with suitable measurement conventions and acknowledge instrument limitations.

**User-friendly description (en):** Measure liquid or gas volumes and recognize the limits of the instruments.

##### Observing Chemical Properties

[observingChemicalProperties.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/measurementsAndEvidence/skills/observingChemicalProperties.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use age-appropriate, adult-led demonstrations or documented observations (for example, iron rusting or a cut apple browning) to identify visible evidence that a material can undergo a chemical change. Have learners describe what changed, distinguish observations from explanations, and connect the evidence to chemical behavior without expecting explanations of reaction mechanisms. Never ask children to taste, smell, heat, or mix unfamiliar substances.

**User-friendly description (en):** Spot signs of chemical change, like iron rusting or a cut apple turning brown.

#### Questions and Models

Skills: 4

[questionsAndModels.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/questionsAndModels/questionsAndModels.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Chemical claims can be examined by specifying substances, observable properties, conditions and possible particle-level explanations.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn how chemical questions are framed and explained using evidence and models.

##### Chemical Models

[chemicalModels.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/questionsAndModels/skills/chemicalModels.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use and critique diagrams, formulas and physical or computational representations according to what they show and omit.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use chemical diagrams and formulas while recognizing what they cannot show.

##### Chemistry as a Discipline

[chemistryAsADiscipline.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/questionsAndModels/skills/chemistryAsADiscipline.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish questions about composition, properties and transformations of matter from neighboring questions about motion, organisms or technological design.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover which questions chemistry can answer about matter and its changes.

##### Macroscopic and Particle Explanations

[macroscopicAndParticleExplanations.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/questionsAndModels/skills/macroscopicAndParticleExplanations.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate an observable change, such as dissolving or gas formation, to a possible account of particles without confusing the model with direct observation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Connect visible chemical changes with possible explanations about particles.

##### Testable Chemical Predictions

[testableChemicalPredictions.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalInquiry/questionsAndModels/skills/testableChemicalPredictions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** State a predicted chemical outcome and the evidence that could support or contradict it.

**User-friendly description (en):** Make a testable prediction about a chemical change and identify supporting evidence.

### Chemical Language and Quantities

Groups: 3 · Skills: 18

[chemicalLanguageAndQuantities.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Chemists represent composition and transformation with conventional symbols and use amounts to connect microscopic entities to measurable samples. This domain covers representational and quantitative relationships, not specific reaction mechanisms.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn the symbols, formulas and calculations chemists use to describe substances and reactions.

#### Amount of Substance

Skills: 6

[amountOfSubstance.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/amountOfSubstance/amountOfSubstance.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The mole and associated quantities link atom-scale counting to bulk mass, volume and reaction proportions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Connect numbers of particles with measurable masses and reaction amounts.

##### Limiting Reactants

[limitingReactants.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/amountOfSubstance/skills/limitingReactants.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Determine which available reactant sets the theoretical upper bound on product formation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Identify which reactant limits the maximum amount of product possible.

##### Mass–Mole Conversion

[massMoleConversion.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/amountOfSubstance/skills/massMoleConversion.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Convert between measured mass and amount of substance for a specified chemical entity.

**User-friendly description (en):** Convert between the mass of a substance and its amount in moles.

##### Molar Mass

[molarMass.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/amountOfSubstance/skills/molarMass.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Connect formula composition to mass per mole using atomic masses.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use molar mass to relate a chemical formula to the mass of a mole.

##### Reaction Yield

[reactionYield.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/amountOfSubstance/skills/reactionYield.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish theoretical yield, observed yield and percentage yield without attributing every shortfall to one cause.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare theoretical and actual reaction yields and explain percentage yield.

##### Stoichiometric Ratios

[stoichiometricRatios.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/amountOfSubstance/skills/stoichiometricRatios.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use balanced coefficients to relate amounts of reactants and products.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use a balanced equation to compare amounts of reactants and products.

##### The Mole

[theMole.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/amountOfSubstance/skills/theMole.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret amount of substance as a count-based quantity defined through Avogadro's constant.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand a mole as a defined number of chemical entities.

#### Chemical Notation

Skills: 8

[chemicalNotation.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/chemicalNotation/chemicalNotation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Symbols and formulas must preserve elemental identity, proportions and charge while being read according to their convention.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how chemical symbols and formulas communicate composition and charge.

##### Chemical Formulas

[chemicalFormulas.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/chemicalNotation/skills/chemicalFormulas.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Read subscripts as composition information rather than reaction coefficients.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how formula subscripts indicate the proportions of different atoms.

##### Element Symbols

[elementSymbols.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/chemicalNotation/skills/elementSymbols.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret standard element symbols and distinguish capitalization changes that create different meanings.

**User-friendly description (en):** Read element symbols correctly, including important differences in capitalization.

##### Empirical Formulas

[empiricalFormulas.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/chemicalNotation/skills/empiricalFormulas.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Derive or interpret the simplest whole-number elemental ratio without assuming that it specifies one molecule.

**User-friendly description (en):** Interpret the simplest whole-number ratio of elements in a substance.

##### Inorganic Nomenclature

[inorganicNomenclature.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/chemicalNotation/skills/inorganicNomenclature.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Apply systematic naming conventions to inorganic compounds, considering ionic or covalent composition and oxidation states where relevant.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use naming rules to identify inorganic compounds.

##### Ionic Compound Formulas

[ionicCompoundFormulas.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/chemicalNotation/skills/ionicCompoundFormulas.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use ion charges to derive electrically neutral formula units.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use ion charges to write formulas for electrically neutral ionic compounds.

##### Molecular Formulas

[molecularFormulas.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/chemicalNotation/skills/molecularFormulas.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret how many atoms of each element are present in a specified discrete molecule.

**User-friendly description (en):** Read a molecular formula to identify the atoms in one molecule.

##### Organic Nomenclature

[organicNomenclature.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/chemicalNotation/skills/organicNomenclature.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use parent structures, locants and functional groups to relate organic compound names to their molecular connectivity.

**User-friendly description (en):** Connect systematic names of organic compounds with their molecular structures.

##### Oxidation States

[oxidationStates.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/chemicalNotation/skills/oxidationStates.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Assign formal oxidation numbers under established conventions without mistaking them for measured atomic charges.

**User-friendly description (en):** Work with formal oxidation numbers without treating them as literal charges.

#### Reaction Equations

Skills: 4

[reactionEquations.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/reactionEquations/reactionEquations.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** An equation records reactants, products and stoichiometric relationships but is not, by itself, a mechanism.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how equations represent chemical transformations and their proportions.

##### Balancing Equations

[balancingEquations.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/reactionEquations/skills/balancingEquations.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Choose coefficients that conserve the number of each element without altering chemical formulas.

**User-friendly description (en):** Balance a chemical equation while keeping the formulas unchanged.

##### Equation State Symbols

[equationStateSymbols.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/reactionEquations/skills/equationStateSymbols.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret notation for solid, liquid, gas and aqueous species as information about conditions or phases.

**User-friendly description (en):** Read symbols showing whether reaction components are solid, liquid, gas or dissolved.

##### Symbolic Equations

[symbolicEquations.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/reactionEquations/skills/symbolicEquations.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Translate a chemical transformation into formulas with correct reactant and product identities.

**User-friendly description (en):** Write chemical formulas that correctly represent reactants and products.

##### Word Equations

[wordEquations.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalLanguageAndQuantities/reactionEquations/skills/wordEquations.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Represent a described change by naming initial and resulting substances.

**User-friendly description (en):** Describe a reaction using the names of its starting substances and products.

### Chemical Reactions

Groups: 3 · Skills: 13

[chemicalReactions.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalReactions/chemicalReactions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** This domain identifies and explains transformations in which constituent atoms are rearranged or electron/proton transfer occurs. Chemical equation notation and amount calculations remain in their dedicated domain.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how chemical reactions change substances by rearranging atoms and transferring particles.

#### Oxidation and Reduction

Skills: 5

[oxidationAndReduction.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalReactions/oxidationAndReduction/oxidationAndReduction.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Electron bookkeeping describes an important class of reactions even when electrons are not explicitly transferred between discrete ions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how oxidation and reduction relate to electron changes.

##### Electrolysis

[electrolysis.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalReactions/oxidationAndReduction/skills/electrolysis.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how externally supplied electrical energy drives non-spontaneous redox reactions at electrodes, including transformations such as electroplating.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how electricity can drive reactions that would not occur spontaneously.

##### Galvanic Cells

[galvanicCells.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalReactions/oxidationAndReduction/skills/galvanicCells.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how spontaneous, spatially separated oxidation and reduction reactions deliver electrical work through an external circuit while charge also flows through the electrolyte.

**User-friendly description (en):** See how separated redox reactions can generate electrical energy in a cell.

##### Oxidation

[oxidation.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalReactions/oxidationAndReduction/skills/oxidation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify increases in formal oxidation state or electron loss in appropriate reaction descriptions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Identify oxidation through electron loss or an increase in oxidation state.

##### Redox Couples

[redoxCouples.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalReactions/oxidationAndReduction/skills/redoxCouples.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate oxidation of one participant to reduction of another and identify oxidizing or reducing agents.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain how one participant is oxidized while another is reduced.

##### Reduction

[reduction.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalReactions/oxidationAndReduction/skills/reduction.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify decreases in formal oxidation state or electron gain in appropriate reaction descriptions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Identify reduction through electron gain or a decrease in oxidation state.

#### Reaction Patterns

Skills: 6

[reactionPatterns.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalReactions/reactionPatterns/reactionPatterns.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Reaction patterns classify transformations such as combination, decomposition, precipitation, displacement, combustion and hydrolysis. Some categories may overlap and do not by themselves determine a detailed reaction mechanism.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover common ways chemical reactions can be classified.

##### Combustion

[combustion.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalReactions/reactionPatterns/skills/combustion.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Characterize reactions with an oxidant that release energy, distinguishing combustion from mere heating.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand combustion as an energy-releasing reaction involving an oxidant.

##### Decomposition Reactions

[decompositionReactions.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalReactions/reactionPatterns/skills/decompositionReactions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize processes in which one chemical species gives rise to multiple products.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when a chemical substance breaks into multiple products.

##### Displacement Reactions

[displacementReactions.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalReactions/reactionPatterns/skills/displacementReactions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Reason about when one element can replace another in a compound.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore when one chemical element can replace another in a compound.

##### Hydrolysis

[hydrolysis.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalReactions/reactionPatterns/skills/hydrolysis.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize reactions in which water participates in bond cleavage or chemical conversion.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize reactions in which water helps break or change chemical bonds.

##### Precipitation Reactions

[precipitationReactions.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalReactions/reactionPatterns/skills/precipitationReactions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain the formation of an insoluble product from reacting dissolved species.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain why a reaction can produce an insoluble solid from dissolved substances.

##### Synthesis Reactions

[synthesisReactions.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalReactions/reactionPatterns/skills/synthesisReactions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize processes producing a new compound from simpler starting substances.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when simpler substances combine to form a new compound.

#### Recognizing Reactions

Skills: 2

[recognizingReactions.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalReactions/recognizingReactions/recognizingReactions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognizing chemical change requires identifying initial and resulting chemical species and examining observations critically rather than treating any visible sign as proof.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn how observations can support a conclusion that a reaction occurred.

##### Reactants and Products

[reactantsAndProducts.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalReactions/recognizingReactions/skills/reactantsAndProducts.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify starting and resulting chemical species while distinguishing them from catalysts and solvents.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish starting reactants and resulting products from catalysts or solvents.

##### Reaction Evidence

[reactionEvidence.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemicalReactions/recognizingReactions/skills/reactionEvidence.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret gas evolution, precipitates, color changes or thermal effects as possible evidence, with appropriate alternative explanations.

**User-friendly description (en):** Assess whether bubbles, colors or temperature changes indicate a chemical reaction.

### Chemistry in the World

Groups: 4 · Skills: 20

[chemistryInTheWorld.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/chemistryInTheWorld.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Chemical concepts support understanding of manufactured materials, environmental systems and molecules associated with life. The emphasis is composition, transformation and evidence—not industrial process engineering, clinical advice or organism-level biology.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how chemistry explains everyday materials, the environment and molecules of life.

#### Air and Water

Skills: 5

[airAndWater.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/airAndWater/airAndWater.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Environmental samples contain reacting or partitioning chemical species whose measurements require attention to concentration and chemical form.

**User-friendly description (en):** Investigate the chemistry of air and water, including pollutants and dissolved materials.

##### Atmospheric Chemical Changes

[atmosphericChemicalChanges.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/airAndWater/skills/atmosphericChemicalChanges.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate pollutant reactions and transformations to phenomena such as acid deposition or photochemical smog.

**User-friendly description (en):** Connect atmospheric chemical reactions with smog and acid deposition.

##### Carbon Chemistry in the Environment

[carbonChemistryInTheEnvironment.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/airAndWater/skills/carbonChemistryInTheEnvironment.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Track carbon among carbon dioxide, dissolved carbonate species and organic matter without conflating chemistry with whole-ecosystem modeling.

**User-friendly description (en):** Track carbon through carbon dioxide, dissolved carbon compounds and organic material.

##### Composition of Air

[compositionOfAir.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/airAndWater/skills/compositionOfAir.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish major atmospheric components from variable traces and pollutants.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize the major gases in air and distinguish them from trace pollutants.

##### Water as a Solvent

[waterAsASolvent.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/airAndWater/skills/waterAsASolvent.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain polarity and hydrogen bonding behind water's distinctive solvent behavior.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore why water dissolves many substances through its molecular interactions.

##### Water Contaminants

[waterContaminants.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/airAndWater/skills/waterContaminants.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Classify dissolved and particulate contaminants by chemical identity and behavior without assuming visible clarity proves safety.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize different water contaminants without assuming clear water is safe.

#### Materials Chemistry

Skills: 7

[materialsChemistry.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/materialsChemistry/materialsChemistry.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A product's useful behavior depends on composition, microscopic structure and conditions of use, not merely its everyday material label.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how chemical structure helps determine a material's useful properties.

##### Alloys in Use

[alloysInUse.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/materialsChemistry/skills/alloysInUse.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how composition and phase structure can change mechanical or corrosion properties relative to constituent metals.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn why alloys can have different properties from the metals they contain.

##### Ceramics

[ceramics.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/materialsChemistry/skills/ceramics.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate inorganic nonmetallic ceramic composition, microstructure and processing to characteristic mechanical and thermal behavior, recognizing that some ceramics contain glassy phases.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how ceramic composition and structure influence strength and heat resistance.

##### Corrosion

[corrosion.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/materialsChemistry/skills/corrosion.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain electrochemical deterioration and the chemical basis of common protective principles.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain how electrochemical reactions cause corrosion and how protection works.

##### Elastomers

[elastomers.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/materialsChemistry/skills/elastomers.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain recoverable deformation in rubberlike polymer networks through chain mobility and cross-linking, without treating all elastic substances as identical plastics.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore why some linked polymer networks can stretch and return to shape.

##### Glass

[glass.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/materialsChemistry/skills/glass.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain the amorphous structure and glass-transition behavior of glass-forming materials, distinguishing them from ordinary crystalline solids.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover why glass behaves differently from crystalline solids.

##### Metals in Use

[metalsInUse.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/materialsChemistry/skills/metalsInUse.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate elemental metallic structure and processing to characteristic conductivity, deformation and corrosion.

**User-friendly description (en):** Connect the structure and processing of metals with their everyday behavior.

##### Plastics

[plastics.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/materialsChemistry/skills/plastics.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate polymer chemistry and processing to the shaping, durability and temperature-dependent behavior of plastic materials.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how polymers and processing influence the properties of plastics.

#### Molecules of Life

Skills: 4

[moleculesOfLife.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/moleculesOfLife/moleculesOfLife.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Chemical structure explains molecular behavior that biology may later place in cellular or organismal context.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore the molecular structures behind important biological materials.

##### Carbohydrate Chemistry

[carbohydrateChemistry.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/moleculesOfLife/skills/carbohydrateChemistry.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate sugar units, glycosidic connections and chemical properties in small and polymeric carbohydrates.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize how sugars join together to form different carbohydrates.

##### Lipid Chemistry

[lipidChemistry.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/moleculesOfLife/skills/lipidChemistry.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize characteristic structures and intermolecular behavior of fats, oils and other lipid families.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare the structures and chemical behavior of fats, oils and other lipids.

##### Nucleic Acid Chemistry

[nucleicAcidChemistry.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/moleculesOfLife/skills/nucleicAcidChemistry.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify nucleotide components and the covalent framework of nucleic acids without teaching genetic inheritance as the primary competency.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand the chemical building blocks and backbone of DNA and RNA.

##### Protein Chemistry

[proteinChemistry.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/moleculesOfLife/skills/proteinChemistry.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate amino-acid connectivity and chemical interactions to protein structure.

**User-friendly description (en):** See how amino acids and their interactions shape protein structure.

#### Sustainable Chemical Choices

Skills: 4

[sustainableChemicalChoices.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/sustainableChemicalChoices/sustainableChemicalChoices.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Environmental and resource decisions benefit from chemical evidence about composition, persistence, transformations and alternatives.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use chemical evidence to make better decisions about materials, waste and resources.

##### Biodegradation and Persistence

[biodegradationAndPersistence.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/sustainableChemicalChoices/skills/biodegradationAndPersistence.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish chemically or biologically degradable compounds from persistent materials under actual environmental conditions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand when substances break down in the environment and when they persist.

##### Chemical Life Cycles

[chemicalLifeCycles.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/sustainableChemicalChoices/skills/chemicalLifeCycles.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Trace a substance through sourcing, use, chemical change and waste streams rather than evaluating one stage in isolation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Trace a chemical substance through production, use and waste rather than examining one step.

##### Green Chemistry Principles

[greenChemistryPrinciples.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/sustainableChemicalChoices/skills/greenChemistryPrinciples.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Evaluate a proposed chemical process by waste prevention, safer inputs, energy demand and material efficiency without assuming any process has zero impact.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare chemical processes by waste, safety, energy needs and material efficiency.

##### Recycling Chemistry

[recyclingChemistry.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/chemistryInTheWorld/sustainableChemicalChoices/skills/recyclingChemistry.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain when chemical composition enables or limits separation, reprocessing and material recovery.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how material composition affects recycling and recovery.

### Energy, Rates and Equilibrium

Groups: 3 · Skills: 19

[energyRatesAndEquilibrium.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/energyRatesAndEquilibrium/energyRatesAndEquilibrium.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Chemical systems exchange energy, evolve at finite rates and may approach dynamic equilibrium. These are related but distinct questions: whether change is favorable, how quickly it occurs and what composition persists.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore energy changes, reaction speeds and the balance between forward and reverse reactions.

#### Chemical Energetics

Skills: 8

[chemicalEnergetics.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/energyRatesAndEquilibrium/chemicalEnergetics/chemicalEnergetics.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Energy changes are properties of a system and its processes, not intrinsic fuel labels or a claim that breaking bonds alone releases energy.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how energy is absorbed, released or redistributed during chemical changes.

##### Bond Energy Estimates

[bondEnergyEstimates.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/energyRatesAndEquilibrium/chemicalEnergetics/skills/bondEnergyEstimates.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Approximate enthalpy changes from bonds broken and formed while recognizing average bond-energy limitations.

**User-friendly description (en):** Estimate reaction energy from bonds broken and formed while recognizing model limits.

##### Calorimetry

[calorimetry.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/energyRatesAndEquilibrium/chemicalEnergetics/skills/calorimetry.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Infer heat transfer from measured temperature change, heat capacity and appropriate system boundaries, recognizing energy losses and measurement uncertainty.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use temperature change to estimate heat transfer, accounting for heat losses.

##### Endothermic Processes

[endothermicProcesses.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/energyRatesAndEquilibrium/chemicalEnergetics/skills/endothermicProcesses.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret positive system enthalpy change and recognize that absorbing heat need not mean a reaction cannot occur.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when a process absorbs heat without assuming it cannot proceed.

##### Entropy

[entropy.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/energyRatesAndEquilibrium/chemicalEnergetics/skills/entropy.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate the multiplicity of microscopic arrangements and energy dispersal to changes in thermodynamic entropy.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how energy dispersal and particle arrangements relate to entropy.

##### Exothermic Processes

[exothermicProcesses.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/energyRatesAndEquilibrium/chemicalEnergetics/skills/exothermicProcesses.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret negative system enthalpy change under stated conditions and distinguish released heat from reaction rate.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when a process releases heat without assuming that it happens quickly.

##### Gibbs Energy

[gibbsEnergy.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/energyRatesAndEquilibrium/chemicalEnergetics/skills/gibbsEnergy.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate enthalpy, temperature and entropy to the direction of spontaneous change at constant temperature and pressure.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use Gibbs energy to judge when a chemical change is favorable under stated conditions.

##### Hess's Law

[hesssLaw.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/energyRatesAndEquilibrium/chemicalEnergetics/skills/hesssLaw.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Combine known reaction equations and associated enthalpy changes to determine an overall enthalpy change using the state-function character of enthalpy.

**User-friendly description (en):** Combine known reaction energy changes to calculate another reaction's enthalpy.

##### Reaction Enthalpy

[reactionEnthalpy.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/energyRatesAndEquilibrium/chemicalEnergetics/skills/reactionEnthalpy.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate heat at constant pressure to the difference in enthalpy between states.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare the energy before and after a reaction using its enthalpy change.

#### Chemical Equilibrium

Skills: 5

[chemicalEquilibrium.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/energyRatesAndEquilibrium/chemicalEquilibrium/chemicalEquilibrium.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Forward and reverse processes may continue while bulk composition becomes steady; equilibrium responds to conditions.
