**Methodological description (English):** Explain bond formation between organic partners accompanied by removal of a small molecule.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how two organic partners join while releasing a small molecule.

##### Elimination Reactions

[eliminationReactions.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/organicChemistry/organicTransformations/skills/eliminationReactions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize removal of atoms or groups with formation of additional unsaturation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain how removing groups can create double or triple bonds.

##### Substitution Reactions

[substitutionReactions.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/organicChemistry/organicTransformations/skills/substitutionReactions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize replacement of one atom or group while retaining much of a carbon skeleton.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when an atom or group is replaced within an organic molecule.

### Particles and States

Groups: 2 · Skills: 18

[particlesAndStates.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/particlesAndStates.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Particle arrangements and motion explain properties of solids, liquids and gases, including transitions between phases. Detailed equations of thermodynamics belong to their own chemical energy competencies.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how the movement and arrangement of particles explain solids, liquids, gases and phase changes.

#### Particle Behavior

Skills: 9

[particleBehavior.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/particleBehavior/particleBehavior.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Models of matter distinguish constituent particles, the spaces between them and their collective motion.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how tiny particles move, interact and make up the materials around us.

##### Diffusion

[diffusion.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/particleBehavior/skills/diffusion.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain net spreading by random particle motion and concentration differences.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain why particles spread from more concentrated to less concentrated regions.

##### Gas Pressure

[gasPressure.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/particleBehavior/skills/gasPressure.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate collisions of gas particles with surfaces to measured pressure and changes in conditions.

**User-friendly description (en):** See how collisions with surfaces create pressure in a gas.

##### Gas Pressure–Temperature Relationship

[gasPressureTemperatureRelationship.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/particleBehavior/skills/gasPressureTemperatureRelationship.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate gas pressure to absolute temperature when volume and gas amount remain fixed under appropriate conditions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how heating a confined gas changes its pressure.

##### Gas Pressure–Volume Relationship

[gasPressureVolumeRelationship.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/particleBehavior/skills/gasPressureVolumeRelationship.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate gas pressure and volume at constant temperature and amount of substance, recognizing the limits of the inverse ideal-gas relationship.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how changing volume affects gas pressure when temperature stays constant.

##### Gas Volume–Amount Relationship

[gasVolumeAmountRelationship.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/particleBehavior/skills/gasVolumeAmountRelationship.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate the volume of a gas to its amount of substance at fixed temperature and pressure under appropriate conditions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Relate gas volume to the amount of gas at constant temperature and pressure.

##### Gas Volume–Temperature Relationship

[gasVolumeTemperatureRelationship.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/particleBehavior/skills/gasVolumeTemperatureRelationship.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate gas volume to absolute temperature when pressure and gas amount remain fixed under appropriate conditions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Connect gas volume with absolute temperature under fixed pressure.

##### Ideal Gas Model

[idealGasModel.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/particleBehavior/skills/idealGasModel.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use the ideal-gas equation as an approximation and identify conditions in which real gases deviate.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use the ideal-gas model while recognizing when it becomes inaccurate.

##### Particle Motion

[particleMotion.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/particleBehavior/skills/particleMotion.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate microscopic movement to spreading, mixing and temperature-dependent behavior.

**User-friendly description (en):** Connect particles' motion with spreading, mixing and temperature changes.

##### Particle Nature of Matter

[particleNatureOfMatter.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/particleBehavior/skills/particleNatureOfMatter.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how an enormous number of microscopic constituents can account for a continuous-looking sample.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain why a sample that looks continuous is made of many tiny particles.

#### Phases and Transitions

Skills: 9

[phasesAndTransitions.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/phasesAndTransitions/phasesAndTransitions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The balance of particle interactions and thermal motion changes whether matter forms a solid, liquid or gas.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover what happens to particles when matter changes between solid, liquid and gas.

##### Condensation

[condensation.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/phasesAndTransitions/skills/condensation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain formation of liquid from vapor as conditions favor a more closely associated particle arrangement.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand why vapor can turn back into liquid droplets.

##### Deposition

[deposition.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/phasesAndTransitions/skills/deposition.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain direct formation of a solid from a vapor without passage through a bulk liquid phase.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain how vapor can form a solid without becoming liquid first.

##### Freezing

[freezing.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/phasesAndTransitions/skills/freezing.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how a liquid transforms into a solid through changes in particle arrangement and energy exchange.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain how cooling can arrange liquid particles into a solid.

##### Gases

[gases.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/phasesAndTransitions/skills/gases.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate compressibility and expansion to widely spaced particles and their motion.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain why gases spread out and can be compressed.

##### Liquids

[liquids.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/phasesAndTransitions/skills/liquids.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate flow and nearly fixed volume to mobile particles that remain close together.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how nearby moving particles allow liquids to flow.

##### Melting

[melting.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/phasesAndTransitions/skills/melting.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how a solid becomes liquid under appropriate temperature and pressure conditions, without requiring a change in chemical identity.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how a solid becomes a liquid without changing into a new substance.

##### Solids

[solids.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/phasesAndTransitions/skills/solids.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate stable shape and structure to constrained particle motion without assuming every solid is crystalline.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain why solids hold their shape even though their particles are not still.

##### Sublimation

[sublimation.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/phasesAndTransitions/skills/sublimation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain direct conversion from solid to vapor without passage through a bulk liquid phase.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain how some solids change directly into vapor.

##### Vaporization

[vaporization.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/particlesAndStates/phasesAndTransitions/skills/vaporization.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain transformation of liquid to gas, distinguishing surface evaporation from boiling within a liquid under suitable pressure.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish evaporation at a surface from boiling throughout a liquid.

### Substances and Properties

Groups: 3 · Skills: 11

[substancesAndProperties.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/substancesAndProperties/substancesAndProperties.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Chemists classify samples by composition and characterize them through reproducible properties. This domain focuses on observable and bulk descriptions before explaining them through atomic structure or bonding.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how chemists identify substances through their composition, properties and changes.

#### Changes and Conservation

Skills: 3

[changesAndConservation.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/substancesAndProperties/changesAndConservation/changesAndConservation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Changes in form and changes in composition are distinct, while matter is conserved in appropriately defined systems.

**User-friendly description (en):** See how changes to matter differ from the creation of new substances.

##### Chemical Changes

[chemicalChanges.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/substancesAndProperties/changesAndConservation/skills/chemicalChanges.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize the formation of new substances, distinguishing reaction evidence from suggestive but inconclusive visual signs.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use appropriate evidence to decide whether a chemical reaction occurred.

##### Mass Conservation

[massConservation.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/substancesAndProperties/changesAndConservation/skills/massConservation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Account for matter in physical and chemical processes, including gases that cross an open-system boundary.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain how matter is conserved even when gases enter or leave a container.

##### Physical Changes

[physicalChanges.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/substancesAndProperties/changesAndConservation/skills/physicalChanges.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize changes in form or phase that do not by themselves establish a different chemical identity.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize melting, cutting and other changes that preserve chemical identity.

#### Characteristic Properties

Skills: 4

[characteristicProperties.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/substancesAndProperties/characteristicProperties/characteristicProperties.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Physical and chemical properties supply different evidence about substances, and measurements are meaningful only under stated conditions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore measurable properties that help describe and identify substances.

##### Chemical Properties

[chemicalProperties.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/substancesAndProperties/characteristicProperties/skills/chemicalProperties.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify how reactivity or resistance to chemical change characterizes a substance under specified conditions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize how a substance's reactivity describes its chemical properties.

##### Density

[density.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/substancesAndProperties/characteristicProperties/skills/density.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate sample mass and volume to an intensive property and use it to distinguish plausible materials.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use mass and volume to reason about a material's density.

##### Physical Properties

[physicalProperties.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/substancesAndProperties/characteristicProperties/skills/physicalProperties.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use density, conductivity, hardness, melting point or other properties that do not require changing chemical identity.

**User-friendly description (en):** Identify properties that can be measured without changing a substance's identity.

##### Property-Based Identification

[propertyBasedIdentification.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/substancesAndProperties/characteristicProperties/skills/propertyBasedIdentification.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Compare multiple measured properties with reference information while acknowledging that one matching property may be insufficient.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare several measured properties to identify a likely substance.

#### Composition

Skills: 4

[composition.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/substancesAndProperties/composition/composition.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A specimen may be a single chemical substance or a combination of substances; its everyday name does not establish its composition.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn to distinguish a single substance from combinations of different substances.

##### Elements and Compounds

[elementsAndCompounds.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/substancesAndProperties/composition/skills/elementsAndCompounds.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish matter containing one element from substances whose constituent elements occur in fixed chemical proportions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish chemical elements from compounds made of different elements.

##### Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Samples

[homogeneousAndHeterogeneousSamples.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/substancesAndProperties/composition/skills/homogeneousAndHeterogeneousSamples.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Classify samples by whether their composition and phases are uniform at the relevant scale.

**User-friendly description (en):** Tell whether a sample is uniform or contains visibly different parts or phases.

##### Mixtures

[mixtures.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/substancesAndProperties/composition/skills/mixtures.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize combinations whose component proportions can vary without making a new substance.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize mixtures whose ingredients can be present in different proportions.

##### Pure Substances

[pureSubstances.data.ts](../../../content/chemistry/data/skills/substancesAndProperties/composition/skills/pureSubstances.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish a chemically defined substance from a sample containing additional components, even when the sample appears uniform.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when a sample is one pure substance rather than a mixture.
